title: Source examples: positioning responses to five forces
rows: Positioning: entering at large scale may improve cost competitiveness, but learning takes time. Differentiation: new products must surpass proven products or offer equivalent performance at lower prices.
A low-cost position may absorb input increases and enable large purchases. Differentiation may support margins and passing on supplier increases when buyers remain brand-loyal.
Cost leadership and price reductions may weaken rivals and alter bargaining power. Differentiated products may reduce customer price sensitivity.
Avoiding price wars may support industry profits. Brand loyalty may reduce price-based competition.
The source suggests investing in substitutes first, acquiring relevant patents and lowering prices to maintain value; it also suggests brand loyalty can reduce trial and switching.
note: These are contextual hypotheses from the notes, not guaranteed outcomes or recommended transactions. The source’s label “consumers” is interpreted here as buyers.

title: TOWS: match internal and external factors
rows: SO: use strengths to take advantage of opportunities. Source label: aggressive/growth-oriented strategy for a favorable match.
WO: overcome weaknesses to pursue opportunities. Source label: turnaround strategy; the final phrase in this image is cropped.
ST: use strengths to avoid threats. Source label: diversification strategy, using current strengths to build long-term opportunities; the ending is cropped.
WT: minimize weaknesses and avoid threats. Source label: defensive strategy; the ending about direct involvement in product markets is cropped.
note: The labels are source interpretations, not exclusive strategic prescriptions. Missing cropped words have not been reconstructed.
